_comment: Canonical Claude plan/session usage-limit banner phrase fragments (card 115c21e7). ERE-safe on purpose -- no \d, no (?:...) -- so the same strings compile unchanged under bash `grep -E`, Python `re`, and JS/TS RegExp. Provenance: card f085fd44 (session-limit alternative from upstream aefa693; the /upgrade STARTUP HINT is deliberately EXCLUDED -- it matched Claude Code's '/upgrade to increase your usage limit.' hint shown in every fresh idle pane, a 2026-06-30 false positive) plus commit 5fccf4f9 (the interactive limit-modal's other two menu options, 'stop and wait for limit to reset' and 'upgrade your plan', added 2026-07-11). Round 2 (2026-09-03, card f4442719, upstream/develop merge): adopted upstream's weekly/session wording widening (measured 2026-08-18: 'reached your weekly limit', 'Approaching Opus weekly limit', 'Session limit reached' were previously silent) -- 'reached your usage limit' widened to 'reached your (usage|weekly) limit', 'approaching (your )?usage limit' widened to 'approaching (your )?(\w+ )?(usage|weekly) limit', and a new '(weekly|session) limit reached' fragment added; the /upgrade token stays excluded. This is the physical source of truth for every consumer EXCEPT src/model-fallback.ts, which keeps its own literal copy (USAGE_LIMIT_FRAGMENTS) for a load-bearing zero-filesystem-dependency reason documented there -- src/__tests__/session-limit-pattern-consistency.test.ts pins the two equal instead. scripts/limit-monitor.sh appends its OWN additional alert-only fragments (rate_limit_error, 429, quota exceeded) on top of this core -- those are intentionally NOT here, because a generic transient rate-limit blip must never trigger a MODEL FALLBACK or a fleet quota-block decision (only a human-facing heads-up alert), a distinction src/model-fallback.ts's own tests pin explicitly.
